text:
The April22,2026 House passage question concerns the whole H.R.6387amendment to the air-quality-monitoring data framework, including exceptional-event definitions, wildfire-mitigation actions, modeling, public petition status, regulatory deadlines, data-use petitions and removal of an interim continuation clause. House passage is not enactment, an approved petition or a finding that particular smoke or weather caused a measured exceedance.
The retained7619baseline establishes air-quality monitoring criteria, stations, daily analysis/reporting and public data reporting. Its subsection(b)exceptional-event definition requires an air-quality effect, an event not reasonably controllable or preventable, the stated event category and an Administrator determination through the regulatory process. The bill changes the event-category limb to natural events, human activities intended to mirror natural events, or human activities unlikely to recur. The other limbs remain: the event still must affect air quality, be not reasonably controllable or preventable, and receive the specified Administrator determination. This is not automatic exceptional-event status for every deliberate ignition. The rewritten exclusions retain ordinarily occurring air-mass stagnation, meteorological inversions and source-noncompliance pollution; the old separate high-temperature/lack-of-precipitation exclusion is removed, which does not itself make every hot or dry period qualifying.
The bill separately defines wildfire-mitigation actions as prescribed fire or similar measures undertaken in accordance with State-approved practices to reduce wildfire risk and severity. It expands the review/handling regulations and listed petition uses to such actions. The amended causal requirement permits a clear causal relationship that exists OR is reasonably expected to exist, linking measured exceedances to the event/action and a specific concentration at a particular monitoring location. Existing reliable/accurate/prompt data and public-process requirements remain; regional modeling is not a blanket automatic approval of every petition.
The Administrator must conduct regional modeling/analysis sufficient for the required demonstration when more than one State notifies intent to petition for the same air-quality event OR the Administrator determines such a multistate event occurred. Those are alternative triggers; actual submission by multiple States is not required for the notification trigger. Proposed regulation revisions are due18monthsafterenactment; final regulations remain due1yearafterpublicationoftheproposal after the retained opportunity for oral presentations. A separate public petition-status website is due12monthsafterenactment and must then be updated monthly. These are distinct clocks, not one deadline or a1yearafterenactment final-rule requirement.
The Governor-petition procedure would reach data directly due to the event/action for the listed exceedance/violation, designation/redesignation/classification/reclassification, Stateattainment demonstration, attainment determination, attainment-date extension, inadequate-implementation-plan and165(a)(3)preconstruction determinations. Exclusion from those regulatory uses does not delete the monitoring record or abolish public access. Retained principles still prioritize public health, timely unhealthy-air information, public database inclusion and Statehealth-protection measures regardless of pollution source. No all-standards waiver or individual project's preconstruction compliance is certified.
The bill strikes subsection(b)(4), the interim continuation clause naming1986guidance,1996PM10guidance and40CFR50AppendicesI/K/N until the effective regulation. This removes that statutory interim clause, not an independently verified repeal of every cited guidance/regulation or a current-enforceability finding. The underlying old guidance, appendices, current implementing rules and particular State-approved practices were not independently inspected; the full retained7619operative unit and own bill, not a current conformed-law or project-specific certificate, ground this candidate.
A Yea supports passage of this whole data/exception/regulatory package; a Nay opposes it without identifying a preferred alternative or component-specific position. NotVoting is a nondirectional observation, not support or opposition. Infrastructure/Technology membership is an UNACCEPTED candidate proposal based on the scientific monitoring-data, mandatory multistate modeling and public status-information channel within the whole measure. A competing boundary treats it as broader environmental air-quality/exception policy. Independent source, whole-package and taxonomy review is required before acceptance/publication. No measured pollution cause, actual petition approval, completed website, reduced wildfire, faster permit, cost saving, health result, motive or accepted domain expansion is inferred.
